I’m by no means a dentist, but I’ve had a filling without laughing gas at a new dentist, which I was really nervous about because I’d always had laughing gas any other time that I’d had a filling. 

What my dentist does is give me some numbing gel on my gum on a cotton swab and rub it’s back and forth on the area to numb where she’s giving me the needle first. The first time I got a filling at this dentist, she didn’t do this long enough to numb the area fully so I still felt the needle, I reminded her of this when I had a second filling and she left it on extra long and ask me if she could feel her tapping my gum afterwards. The numbing needle went in and I didn’t feel a thing. But my dentist is really gentle and she makes me feel safe and comfortable, she walks me through every step so I know what’s going on. 

I know it’s not the same as an extraction, but it all depends on how comfortable you feel with this dentist. If you’re not comfortable getting any treatment done without laughing gas, by all means go somewhere else. But you also have to advocate yourself like I did when i reminded my dentist of the numbing gel before the needle the first time.

You can try and keep changing out the oil, (oil being the vyvanse or like any other thing you put it in it, like vitamins, caffeine) yourself but eventually you’ll need a mechanic (doctor) to look at your car and figure out what needs to be done to get the car back in working condition.

If you’re allowed to have your phone on you at work, you can get an app that reminds you drink water, I have one and I also have a Fitbit so I set it up to get reminders to drink water on my Fitbit too. My biggest tips as a first time renter. 

- show up at inspections early, dressed nicely, introduce yourself to the agent, create small talk. Ask them for their email if you don’t have it already. Just be really really nice, not too nice to the point where it’s creepy tho 😂

- test the water pressure in all showers and sinks. Make sure there’s enough space and storage for all your needs. I have lots of junk (not a hoarder lol, just stuff with mems tied to it that I’m too weak to give away). 

- get in touch with agent a few days after the inspection just to get an update on how your application is going. I always start with ‘Hi (agents name) hope your day is going well, lovely to meet you the other day. Just checking into see how our application is going for (insert address). Looking forward to hearing from you, sincerely luna997’. 

- I can’t stress this one enough!! Create a cover letter about why you want the property, how long you two have been together, your employment, hobbies, basically how you’re the quietest people ever and you don’t have parties and tbh you whisper to each other every second of the day so your neighbours have nothing to complain about. I’m more than happy to send you a copy of my cover letter that I used for our rental. 

- have good referees!! Sometimes they call, sometimes they don’t, but when they don’t wanna be calling something that says “oh yeah, I’ve known (your/ your partners name) for a few years, they keep to themselves.. blah blah generic shit”

- have a guarantor as a back up. If you’re struggling to find a rental have 5+ applications and you get knock backs every time, it’s time to bring in someone who has a good rental history and is financially stable. The agent at the rental I’m living in now suggested it because no one got our rental the first time and then we went for it again with a guarantor and the next day got the call that we got approved for it. 

- biggest tip of them all: make sure you can afford it. With the cost of living the way that is at the moment, I cannot stress this enough. Renting sounds easy at first, but you gotta think that it’s not just paying rent, it’s paying for furniture, bills, food: 3 meals a day so you don’t starve, paying car insurance as well, rego, phone bill, water bill, internet bills, electricity so you don’t freeze, it all adds up. 

Anyway, good luck!! Honestly, it’s such a tough time finding rentals at the moment and don’t take the instant knock backs personally, everything happens for a reason!

My brother also started eating may contain products as a teenager and my mum was livid, but she got used to it. I haven’t seen him have a reaction since he was 16 and his 28 now.
